notes: Starting point compiled from public guidance, NOT verified by the AuraFlashXR project on this headset (no `verified` entry). AuraFlashXR's support for headsets other than the Apple Vision Pro is best effort.

Quest 2, 3 and 3S share this profile except for the panel size (2064 x 2208 per eye here): they all stream HEVC with AuraFlashXR's Android client and a Qualcomm Snapdragon XR2 decoder (Quest 3 and 3S: XR2 Gen 2; Quest 2: XR2 Gen 1). Against the Apple Vision Pro profile (3552 x 3200, 300 Mbps, split encoding) the stream has 2-2.4x fewer pixels and needs about half the bitrate. Same as on the Vision Pro: 90 Hz, HEVC 10-bit (the default session forces it; AuraFlashXR's Quest client advertises 10-bit support), full colour range; chroma-key passthrough is off by default (the setup offers it, key colour pure green #00FF00). Foveation is AuraFlashXR's 'Light' preset (centre 0.80 x 0.80, edge ratio 8 x 8): nearly the whole view stays at full resolution, the saving is small on purpose.

AuraFlashXR wiki (based on AuraFlashXR's) (Settings tutorial, v20): on a good wireless router use the medium resolution preset (the default) with sharpening 1.0 and HEVC at a constant 100-150 Mbps; HEVC is usually the best codec when bitrate is limited; turn foveated encoding on and tune it from the statistics graph.
Resolution, gamma and the encoder details are left out on purpose: the headset's own default (what AuraFlashXR reports at the handshake) is used. Change them in the wizard if you know better.
Résolution optimale par défaut configurée à 2496 x 2608 par œil ; fréquences de rafraîchissement supportées : 72 / 80 / 90 / 120 / 144 / 207 Hz (120 Hz par défaut).
Support complet des codecs H.264 (AVC), HEVC (H.265) et AV1 sur les GPU RTX 4000 / 5000 via les paramètres avancés.
